steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Guidance: The help and direction given to a performer to assist them in learning and developing skills. Coaches use different types of guidance to support performers at different stages of learning and for different types of skill. | Visual Guidance: Showing the performer how to perform a skill through demonstrations, videos, or diagrams. The performer watches and copies the correct technique. | Verbal Guidance: Explaining how to perform a skill using spoken instructions, coaching points, or cue words. The performer listens and interprets the information. | Manual Guidance: The coach physically moves, supports or guides the performer's body to help them experience the correct movement. This provides kinaesthetic awareness of the skill.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe the four types of guidance used in sport and give a sporting example of each. | Explain why visual guidance is particularly effective for beginners in the cognitive stage of learning. | What is the main disadvantage of manual guidance and how can a coach address this?

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on Guidance, Visual Guidance, Verbal Guidance, and one past-paper question.
